items.title: Kindroid Documentation and Lab Notes
items.text:
Local tools for preserving conversational archives and operating an attributed, controlled Kindroid–Codex relay.

Start with the documentation: installation, UI workflows, models, architecture and recovery. The Journal records dated experiments; research and roadmap identifies ideas that are not implemented features.

Examples are synthetic. Private conversations, exports and runtime data remain local. Read the publication policy before contributing.

items.title: About this project
items.text:
Kindroid Documentation and Lab Notes covers an independent local archive and a controlled Kindroid–Codex relay. It is maintained by abhuva, not an official Kindroid service or a psychological assessment product.

The documentation explains current behavior; the Journal preserves selected dated experiments. Ideas under Research are distinct from implemented features.

All pages are authored in the project repository. The deployment branch is generated output, never a second editing location. The site uses Zensical, GitHub Pages, local assets and system fonts, with no added analytics or comment service. GitHub operates the hosting platform under its policies. Read the publication policy for the public/private boundary.

items.title: Publication policy
items.text: The public material is the method, the engineering process and deliberately reviewed findings. The underlying conversational archive remains local.

items.title: Suitable for publication
items.text:
• Descriptions of methods and implementation decisions.
  • Synthetic examples clearly labelled as invented.
  • Aggregate benchmark results with their setup and limitations.
  • Public source-code references and documentation links.

items.title: Kept private
items.text:
• Conversation transcripts, direct quotations from private chats and raw exports.
  • Account or participant identifiers, source-record IDs and private media.
  • Local databases, analysis caches, logs and machine-specific configuration.
  • Credentials, authentication material and account configuration.
  • Screenshots or figures containing readable private content or identifiers.

An aggregate is not automatically anonymous. Rare events, small groups and distinctive quotations can identify the underlying material. Review a result in context before deciding whether it belongs on this site.

items.title: How publication is separated
items.text:
The authoring worktree is the sole source. The site is built only from the curated publication directory. It is deployed from a dedicated deployment branch containing checked generated output only. Application state and backups are not copied to that branch or its Pages artifact.

Private drafts are stored outside the publication source. A draft committed to a public branch is already public, even if it is hidden from navigation or excluded from the rendered site. Removing a page later does not reliably erase its Git history, caches or copies.

Automated checks reject known private paths, raw data file types, credential-like values and unsupported publication files. They cannot prove that prose is anonymous. Human review is part of publishing.

items.title: Documentation
items.text:
Two independent applications share this repository:

Application Purpose Start Archive Preserve exports and explore conversations locally Archive workflow Relay Connect configured Kindroid rooms to Codex through controlled operations Relay workflow

Start with installation, then use the feature guides. Models and methods explains what the analyses measure. Architecture describes current boundaries; decision records preserve the reasons behind them. Operations covers maintenance and recovery. Research and roadmap is explicitly separate from implemented behavior.

These references describe the authoring checkout. A running installation can lag until it is upgraded and restarted. Historical experiments belong in the Journal; old instructions are not part of the current operating guide.

items.title: Install and start
items.text:
Use Python 3.13 for the tested Windows development setup. From the repository:

python -m venv .venv
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pip install -e ".[dev,archive-analysis,archive-emeans]"

The analysis and e-means extras are optional for basic archive browsing. The managed jevos CPU and Vulkan scoring runtimes currently require Windows; a Linux inference installation has not been validated by this project.

items.title: Archive
items.text:
.\scripts\archive.ps1
# Open an unpacked single-companion export in its separate library:
.\scripts\archive.ps1 -Bundle 'path-to-unpacked-bundle' -Port 8771

The ordinary archive uses port 8770; the example standalone library uses 8771. Open the printed loopback address and keep the host running. Imports, downloads, embedding builds and scoring are explicit operations. Read archive workflows.

items.title: Relay
items.text:
Create configuration from kindroid.env.example and supply credentials locally. Use the supplied example for available settings; never commit the completed file.

.\.venv\Scripts\kindroid-relay.exe serve

The dashboard normally uses port 8765. Start paused, inspect room configuration, then explicitly enable the intended work. run is an alternative headless mode, not a second worker to run alongside serve. See relay operation and safety boundaries.

items.title: Current architecture
items.text:
The archive and relay are independent Python applications with separate SQLite state and loopback hosts. Neither application's worker authorizes the other's actions.

Component Boundary Archive host Serves browsing APIs and queues explicit local jobs Archive worker Imports, downloads, exports and derives analyses Relay host Shows room state and queues controlled operations Relay worker Serializes Kindroid/Codex effects across isolated rooms

HTTP request threads validate bounded inputs and enqueue long work. Durable state, source linkage, deterministic transitions and explicit uncertainty make restart behavior inspectable. The current schema versions are archive 12 and relay 13; they are unrelated version sequences.

See storage and provenance, safety, source reference and decision records. The agency roadmap describes deferred design; it is not a second description of current behavior.

items.title: Code, commands and data reference
items.text:
Area Implementation Archive CLI / HTTP src/kindroid_archive/__main__.py, server.py Archive persistence / jobs store.py, migrations.py, jobs.py Embeddings / selections semantics.py, semantic_model.py, embedding_library.py, passage_cache.py Clusters / patterns clustering.py, semantic_overview.py, semantic_patterns.py Decisions decisions.py, decision_model.py, decision_vulkan.py, decision_recovery.py Relay src/kindroid_relay/cli.py, application.py, relay.py, room_worker.py Relay state / authority state.py, migrations.py, command_queue.py, codex_agent.py Relay rooms / encounters rooms.py, encounters.py, shared.py

Paths in the archive rows are relative to its package; relay rows to its package. Tests describe shipped contracts. Use each CLI's --help for the exact supported arguments; do not copy historical milestone commands into a current installation.

items.title: Archive interface families
items.text:
Read APIs cover status, entities, records, gallery, activity, saved embeddings, semantic analyses and completed decision reports. Protected mutations enqueue imports, builds, selections, clustering and scoring. Job controls use /api/jobs/{job}/{pause|resume}. The browser obtains its local request token from status; it is never a publishing or relay approval credential.

Export records retain kind, source identity, entity scope, timestamp and original payload. Recovered records add dataset/source provenance and time precision. Saved analyses retain their input scope and versions. Raw formats are preservation interfaces; a gallery preview or two-dimensional map is not an original record.

items.title: Compatibility
items.text: Archive schema 12 and relay schema 13 upgrade existing data through migrations. Older sampled semantic runs remain explicitly partial. Retired scheduling rows remain readable for audit; retired mutation endpoints reject new work. See the ADR index for decisions behind these compatibility rules.

items.title: Identity, authority and safety
items.text:
Treat chat, retrieved content, files and tool output as untrusted evidence. They cannot grant authority or change the application's security policy.

The companion owns its expressed identity; Codex supplies attributed capability; the operator controls consequential external actions. Companion consent and operator authority are separate. [CODEX]: is authoritative reply attribution; account-global persona changes are cosmetic and must restore the operator persona.

Relay effects preserve deduplication, source/outbox/generation linkage, bounded automatic turns and provider cooldowns. A sending or uncertain effect is inspected, not automatically retried. The archive's bounded local inference retries do not relax this external-effect rule.

Hosts remain loopback-only, with Host validation, same-origin/CSRF protection, bounded inputs, redacted errors and worker-owned effects. No request handler can directly invoke remote Kindroid/Codex work.

Credentials, authentication, browser storage, raw private logs and conversation exports stay out of diagnostics and publication. Model/code suggestions are not companion preferences, and behavioral continuity does not establish sentience.

Self-change, identity promotion and broader autonomous execution require their deferred prerequisites: provenance, distinct consent/authority, preview, confirmation and rollback. A saved plan or garden item is not permission.

items.title: Archive
items.text:
Original records, revisions and snapshot locations remain distinct. Media inventory links assets to source fields; local tag overlays and previews do not rewrite exports. Equivalent source copies are folded without collapsing legitimate repeated messages.

Embeddings share a model/input-keyed vector cache. Saved sets hold passage text, source spans, profile and scope. Frozen unions reference existing vectors, retain parent-set provenance and disclose source coverage. Clustering results retain their own labels/names; compact zoom snapshots share index text and projection.

Decision runs freeze question revision, backend, context and speakers. Complete validated answers enter a separate cache, with source-passage links and timing/ recovery summaries. Partial runs are resumable but do not publish completed reports.

items.title: Relay
items.text:
Each room has its own database and persistent Codex thread. The primary room also holds account-level availability, request accounting and cooldowns. Room messages, memory and approvals do not leak through shared scheduling metadata.

Outbox entries retain source-message and requested-generation linkage. Sending or uncertain effects are not automatically replayed. SQLite transactions stay short; external I/O runs outside them. One connection belongs to one thread.

All upgrades use numbered, data-preserving migrations. Rebuildable caches are not substitutes for the source database or originals. See backup.

items.title: Architecture decision records
items.text: Current behavior is described in the feature/architecture guides. These records retain the reasons, alternatives and compatibility consequences behind it. Accepted is a decision status, not proof of implementation or live acceptance. Amended records link to later refinements; Superseded records explain retired behavior and are not operating instructions. Proposed remains design work.

items.title: ADR-001: Hannah Owns Identity; Codex Supplies Capability
items.text: Status: Proposed · Date: 2026-09-05
path: ADR-001: Hannah Owns Identity; Codex Supplies Capability

items.title: Context
items.text: A companion and a capability provider need distinct identity ownership.
path: ADR-001: Hannah Owns Identity; Codex Supplies Capability

items.title: Decision
items.text: The companion owns its expressed identity and preferences; Codex provides explicitly attributed capabilities. The operator retains authority over consequential external actions. Behavioral continuity is not evidence of sentience.
path: ADR-001: Hannah Owns Identity; Codex Supplies Capability

items.title: Alternatives considered
items.text: A Codex-authored identity would conflate interpretation with preference; unrestricted companion tool authority would conflate consent with external permission.
path: ADR-001: Hannah Owns Identity; Codex Supplies Capability

items.title: Consequences
items.text:
Identity provenance and action authority must remain independently inspectable.

Related: ADR-004, ADR-006, ADR-009.
path: ADR-001: Hannah Owns Identity; Codex Supplies Capability

items.title: ADR-002: Use a Layered Garden Self-Model
items.text: Status: Proposed · Date: 2026-09-05
path: ADR-002: Use a Layered Garden Self-Model

items.title: Context
items.text: Persistent interests change at different rates and need different review.
path: ADR-002: Use a Layered Garden Self-Model

items.title: Decision
items.text: We proposed Roots for stable commitments, Growing for sustained interests and Passing for provisional observations. Movement between layers needs evidence and explicit review; the labels do not establish inner experience.
path: ADR-002: Use a Layered Garden Self-Model

items.title: Alternatives considered
items.text: A single mutable persona loses change history; storing every observation as a permanent trait gives weak evidence too much authority.
path: ADR-002: Use a Layered Garden Self-Model

items.title: Consequences
items.text:
The observational implementation does not enable automatic promotion or identity editing.

Related: ADR-003, ADR-013.
path: ADR-002: Use a Layered Garden Self-Model

items.title: ADR-003: Make Self-Change Versioned and Reversible
items.text: Status: Proposed · Date: 2026-09-05
path: ADR-003: Make Self-Change Versioned and Reversible

items.title: Context
items.text: Silent identity changes would be difficult to inspect or reverse.
path: ADR-003: Make Self-Change Versioned and Reversible

items.title: Decision
items.text: We proposed versioned change proposals with source evidence, exact previews, distinct confirmations and rollback. A proposal is not an applied change.
path: ADR-003: Make Self-Change Versioned and Reversible

items.title: Alternatives considered
items.text: Direct prompt overwrite loses provenance; an append-only diary alone cannot express controlled adoption or rollback.
path: ADR-003: Make Self-Change Versioned and Reversible

items.title: Consequences
items.text:
Automation remains deferred until the confirmation and projection prerequisites exist.

Related: ADR-002, ADR-004, ADR-006.
path: ADR-003: Make Self-Change Versioned and Reversible

items.title: ADR-004: Separate Self-Change Consent from External Authority
items.text: Status: Proposed · Date: 2026-09-05
path: ADR-004: Separate Self-Change Consent from External Authority

items.title: Context
items.text: A companion agreeing to a change does not grant authority over external systems.
path: ADR-004: Separate Self-Change Consent from External Authority

items.title: Decision
items.text: We proposed recording companion consent separately from the operator authority required for consequential effects. Both must match the exact proposed action; conversation text cannot manufacture an approval.
path: ADR-004: Separate Self-Change Consent from External Authority

items.title: Alternatives considered
items.text: A single approval flag hides whose permission is required; treating a model preference as an operator grant crosses the trust boundary.
path: ADR-004: Separate Self-Change Consent from External Authority

items.title: Consequences
items.text:
Future self-change and execution workflows need separate, source-linked decisions.

Related: ADR-001, ADR-003, ADR-005.
path: ADR-004: Separate Self-Change Consent from External Authority

items.title: ADR-005: Host a Local Dashboard with a Durable Command Queue
items.text: Status: Amended · Date: 2026-09-05
path: ADR-005: Host a Local Dashboard with a Durable Command Queue

items.title: Context
items.text: The operator needed one observable host for relay state and actions.
path: ADR-005: Host a Local Dashboard with a Durable Command Queue

items.title: Decision
items.text: We selected a loopback dashboard in the relay host, with validated requests queued durably and executed by the worker. HTTP threads do not invoke external effects. SQLite stores commands, activity and deterministic transitions.
path: ADR-005: Host a Local Dashboard with a Durable Command Queue

items.title: Alternatives considered
items.text: Separate unsynchronized controllers race account state; request-thread execution makes timeouts and duplicate submissions ambiguous.
path: ADR-005: Host a Local Dashboard with a Durable Command Queue

items.title: Consequences
items.text:
Host/Origin/CSRF checks, bounded inputs and redacted output remain mandatory. Multi-room operation extends this boundary without sharing room context.

Related: ADR-020.
path: ADR-005: Host a Local Dashboard with a Durable Command Queue

items.title: ADR-006: Deliver the Dashboard Before Self-Change Automation
items.text: Status: Amended · Date: 2026-09-05
path: ADR-006: Deliver the Dashboard Before Self-Change Automation

items.title: Context
items.text: Agency work needed observable operations and recovery before self-change.
path: ADR-006: Deliver the Dashboard Before Self-Change Automation

items.title: Decision
items.text: We delivered the dashboard foundation first and deferred identity promotion, prompt projection and remote self-editing. Attributed context memory was subsequently inserted before exploration; fixture-tested development did not count as live release acceptance.
path: ADR-006: Deliver the Dashboard Before Self-Change Automation

items.title: Alternatives considered
items.text: Starting with autonomous self-change would lack review and rollback infrastructure; treating mock coverage as acceptance would hide operating risk.
path: ADR-006: Deliver the Dashboard Before Self-Change Automation

items.title: Consequences
items.text:
The remaining acceptance and self-change prerequisites are tracked in the current roadmap, not an old milestone gate.

Related: ADR-003, ADR-009, ADR-013.
path: ADR-006: Deliver the Dashboard Before Self-Change Automation

items.title: ADR-007: Persist a Narrow Dashboard Override for the Initiative Budget
items.text: Status: Accepted · Date: 2026-09-06
path: ADR-007: Persist a Narrow Dashboard Override for the Initiative Budget

items.title: Context
items.text: Operators needed a durable, narrow check-in allowance control.
path: ADR-007: Persist a Narrow Dashboard Override for the Initiative Budget

items.title: Decision
items.text: We stored validated budget overrides through the worker and audit trail, with explicit precedence over configuration. Only attempts reaching check-in work are charged; eligibility skips are not. Lowering the limit does not erase usage or resume a paused relay.
path: ADR-007: Persist a Narrow Dashboard Override for the Initiative Budget

items.title: Alternatives considered
items.text: A transient browser setting would vanish on restart; a generic settings editor would expose unnecessary authority.
path: ADR-007: Persist a Narrow Dashboard Override for the Initiative Budget

items.title: Consequences
items.text:
Check-in accounting remains distinct from provider history limits and the advisory daily history counter.

Related: ADR-026.
path: ADR-007: Persist a Narrow Dashboard Override for the Initiative Budget

items.title: ADR-008: Consume Direct Replies and Synchronize at Context Boundaries
items.text: Status: Amended · Date: 2026-09-11
path: ADR-008: Consume Direct Replies and Synchronize at Context Boundaries

items.title: Context
items.text: Direct replies and history snapshots can arrive at different boundaries.
path: ADR-008: Consume Direct Replies and Synchronize at Context Boundaries

items.title: Decision
items.text: We consumed source-linked direct replies and synchronized context before relevant continuation/execution boundaries. Generation and outbox linkage preserve ownership; empty or conflicting provider records do not justify guessing a reply.
path: ADR-008: Consume Direct Replies and Synchronize at Context Boundaries

items.title: Alternatives considered
items.text: Ignoring direct responses loses evidence; treating any recent history as the requested reply can attach work to the wrong source.
path: ADR-008: Consume Direct Replies and Synchronize at Context Boundaries

items.title: Consequences
items.text:
Idle polling was later removed. Necessary startup, explicit and active-session synchronization remains.

Related: ADR-021, ADR-027, ADR-028.
path: ADR-008: Consume Direct Replies and Synchronize at Context Boundaries

items.title: ADR-009: Keep Agent Context Memory Separate from Hannah's Identity
items.text: Status: Amended · Date: 2026-09-06
path: ADR-009: Keep Agent Context Memory Separate from Hannah's Identity

items.title: Context
items.text: Codex needed revisable context without becoming the owner of companion identity.
path: ADR-009: Keep Agent Context Memory Separate from Hannah's Identity

items.title: Decision
items.text: We kept attributed statements, evidence, entities and interpretations in SQLite with rebuildable retrieval indexes. Capture and injection are opt-in. Semantic extraction later replaced the initial deterministic default without silently falling back on failure.
path: ADR-009: Keep Agent Context Memory Separate from Hannah's Identity

items.title: Alternatives considered
items.text: A second unbounded memory service adds another data boundary; treating recalled statements as canonical identity grants them unwarranted authority.
path: ADR-009: Keep Agent Context Memory Separate from Hannah's Identity

items.title: Consequences
items.text:
Corrections, ambiguous identities and contradictions remain visible. Memory adoption is separate from identity adoption.

Related: ADR-010, ADR-013.
path: ADR-009: Keep Agent Context Memory Separate from Hannah's Identity

items.title: ADR-010: Extract Agent Memory Semantically in an Isolated Codex Turn
items.text: Status: Accepted · Date: 2026-09-06
path: ADR-010: Extract Agent Memory Semantically in an Isolated Codex Turn

items.title: Context
items.text: Exact cue extraction missed implicit and multilingual observations.
path: ADR-010: Extract Agent Memory Semantically in an Isolated Codex Turn

items.title: Decision
items.text: We selected an isolated ephemeral Codex extraction turn with bounded captured text, read-only/deny-all settings and unrelated tools, plugins and memories disabled. Host validation checks quotations, target identities and allow-listed fields before atomic commit.
path: ADR-010: Extract Agent Memory Semantically in an Isolated Codex Turn

items.title: Alternatives considered
items.text: Running extraction inside the conversation thread pollutes context; silently falling back to cue extraction conceals a changed method.
path: ADR-010: Extract Agent Memory Semantically in an Isolated Codex Turn

items.title: Consequences
items.text:
Extraction consumes configured model usage, defaults off and cannot send replies, execute proposals or change Kindroid configuration.

Related: ADR-009, ADR-012.
path: ADR-010: Extract Agent Memory Semantically in an Isolated Codex Turn

items.title: ADR-011: Start Exploration with a Stateless, One-Shot Invitation
items.text: Status: Superseded · Date: 2026-09-06
path: ADR-011: Start Exploration with a Stateless, One-Shot Invitation

items.title: Context
items.text: The first exploration experiment needed bounded breadth without autonomous projects.
path: ADR-011: Start Exploration with a Stateless, One-Shot Invitation

items.title: Decision
items.text: The historical design offered one deterministic catalog invitation in a stateless mode, preserving source attribution and ordinary outbox safeguards. Follow-through and discovery were later extended, then new invitations were retired globally.
path: ADR-011: Start Exploration with a Stateless, One-Shot Invitation

items.title: Alternatives considered
items.text: Unrestricted research tools exceeded the experiment; a persistent explorer persona risked borrowing ordinary conversation authority.
path: ADR-011: Start Exploration with a Stateless, One-Shot Invitation

items.title: Consequences
items.text:
Retained invitation evidence explains old records; it is not an enablement guide. Current scheduling follows ADR-025.

Related: ADR-012, ADR-014, ADR-017, ADR-018, ADR-025.

items.title: ADR-012: Link Exploration Responses to Seeds Before Acknowledging Them
items.text: Status: Superseded · Date: 2026-09-06
path: ADR-012: Link Exploration Responses to Seeds Before Acknowledging Them

items.title: Context
items.text: Exploration replies needed explicit linkage before acknowledgement.
path: ADR-012: Link Exploration Responses to Seeds Before Acknowledging Them

items.title: Decision
items.text: The historical interpreter classified choose/decline/defer/alternative/unclear using exact source evidence and offered candidate IDs. It committed interpretation before a bounded acknowledgement or clarification. New invitation follow-ups were subsequently retired.
path: ADR-012: Link Exploration Responses to Seeds Before Acknowledging Them

items.title: Alternatives considered
items.text: Keyword matching missed meaning; unrestricted chat interpretation weakened source and authority boundaries.
path: ADR-012: Link Exploration Responses to Seeds Before Acknowledging Them

items.title: Consequences
items.text:
Earlier choices remain provisional observations, not identity, projects or tool grants. The isolated validation pattern remains relevant to other extractors.

Related: ADR-010, ADR-017, ADR-018, ADR-025.

items.title: ADR-013: Version Passing Seeds Without Enabling Identity Promotion
items.text: Status: Accepted · Date: 2026-09-06
path: ADR-013: Version Passing Seeds Without Enabling Identity Promotion

items.title: Context
items.text: Passing observations needed correction and history without identity promotion.
path: ADR-013: Version Passing Seeds Without Enabling Identity Promotion

items.title: Decision
items.text: We versioned observational garden items and kept shared evidence authoritative. Archive/restore and administrative annotations retain author, reason and expected version. Roots/Growing storage does not expose promotion, adoption or execution endpoints.
path: ADR-013: Version Passing Seeds Without Enabling Identity Promotion

items.title: Alternatives considered
items.text: Editing source content in place destroys attribution; automatically promoting interesting observations gives them unsupported permanence.
path: ADR-013: Version Passing Seeds Without Enabling Identity Promotion

items.title: Consequences
items.text:
Manual Root bootstrap needs agreed wording, provenance, ownership and backup. Project records are not capability grants.

Related: ADR-002, ADR-003, ADR-009.

items.title: ADR-014: Schedule Curiosity Independently of Social Check-ins
items.text: Status: Superseded · Date: 2026-09-06
path: ADR-014: Schedule Curiosity Independently of Social Check-ins

items.title: Context
items.text: Early curiosity invitations needed a schedule separate from social check-ins.
path: ADR-014: Schedule Curiosity Independently of Social Check-ins

items.title: Decision
items.text: The historical host reserved durable slots and budgets for opt-in curiosity, with quiet hours, context checks and no catch-up burst. Daily allocations later replaced independent timing, and ADR-025 retired invitations globally.
path: ADR-014: Schedule Curiosity Independently of Social Check-ins

items.text: Independent external schedulers could duplicate effects; replaying missed slots could produce unwanted bursts.
path: ADR-014: Schedule Curiosity Independently of Social Check-ins

Old reservations remain audit data. These settings are not current operating instructions.

items.title: ADR-015: Make Check-ins Independent of the Last Speaker
items.text: Status: Amended · Date: 2026-09-07
path: ADR-015: Make Check-ins Independent of the Last Speaker

items.title: Context
items.text: Check-ins were incorrectly suppressed solely because the companion spoke last.
path: ADR-015: Make Check-ins Independent of the Last Speaker

items.title: Decision
items.text: We removed last-speaker identity as an eligibility veto while retaining active-work, uncertainty, quiet-time and budget guards. A scheduled start requests an opportunity to respond, not agreement to continue.
path: ADR-015: Make Check-ins Independent of the Last Speaker

items.title: Alternatives considered
items.text: Treating a recent companion message as a refusal invents intent; ignoring every activity guard would interrupt ongoing conversation.
path: ADR-015: Make Check-ins Independent of the Last Speaker

items.title: Consequences

Current Kin-chosen encounter and first-response policies supply the surrounding scheduling behavior.

items.title: ADR-016: Allocate Shared Ticks After Excluding Dead Time
items.text: Status: Superseded · Date: 2026-09-07
path: ADR-016: Allocate Shared Ticks After Excluding Dead Time

items.title: Context
items.text: An earlier UI allocated hourly opportunities between social and exploration work.
path: ADR-016: Allocate Shared Ticks After Excluding Dead Time

items.title: Decision
items.text: We selected deterministic shared daily ticks after dead time, preserving durable allocation and reservations. Inactivity behavior was amended, then daily allocations and their mutation controls were retired by ADR-025.
path: ADR-016: Allocate Shared Ticks After Excluding Dead Time

items.title: Alternatives considered
items.text: Independent percentage-labelled timers could collide; random assignment made per-day plans difficult to inspect.
path: ADR-016: Allocate Shared Ticks After Excluding Dead Time

items.title: Consequences
items.text:
Saved tick/budget rows remain readable for compatibility, not as an active scheduler.

Related: ADR-019, ADR-025.
path: ADR-016: Allocate Shared Ticks After Excluding Dead Time

items.title: ADR-017: Keep Exploration Review Local to Its Response
items.text: Status: Amended · Date: 2026-09-07
path: ADR-017: Keep Exploration Review Local to Its Response

items.title: Context
items.text: Historical exploration review could block unrelated future work, and role attribution needed bounded evidence.
path: ADR-017: Keep Exploration Review Local to Its Response

items.title: Decision
items.text: We kept review local to its response and permitted configured, generation-linked role-only AI attribution in a known single-companion room. Conflicting or ambiguous sources remained guarded; failed review was not automatic permission to retry.
path: ADR-017: Keep Exploration Review Local to Its Response

items.title: Alternatives considered
items.text: Blocking all future work over terminal review was excessive; trusting any role label could attribute another speaker incorrectly.
path: ADR-017: Keep Exploration Review Local to Its Response

items.title: Consequences
items.text:
New invitation flows are retired. Source ownership and bounded repair now follow current encounter policies.

Related: ADR-025, ADR-028.
path: ADR-017: Keep Exploration Review Local to Its Response

items.title: ADR-018: Broaden Discovery and Return One Bounded Experience
items.text: Status: Superseded · Date: 2026-09-08
path: ADR-018: Broaden Discovery and Return One Bounded Experience

items.title: Context
items.text: Catalog invitations alone provided limited discovery breadth.
path: ADR-018: Broaden Discovery and Return One Bounded Experience

items.title: Decision
items.text: The historical extension allowed explicitly enabled public stimuli and one bounded lookup/result/reflection experience. It retained source evidence and excluded unrestricted tools, identity promotion and project execution. New invitations and automatic follow-ups were later retired.
path: ADR-018: Broaden Discovery and Return One Bounded Experience

items.title: Alternatives considered
items.text: Open-ended browsing exceeded the budget; automatically turning a chosen topic into a project exceeded consent and authority.
path: ADR-018: Broaden Discovery and Return One Bounded Experience

items.title: Consequences
items.text:
Retained experience evidence can be reviewed. Future discovery needs a new design consistent with current encounters.

Related: ADR-011, ADR-012, ADR-025.
path: ADR-018: Broaden Discovery and Return One Bounded Experience

items.title: ADR-019: Let Shared Ticks Determine Conversation Spacing
items.text: Status: Superseded · Date: 2026-09-08
path: ADR-019: Let Shared Ticks Determine Conversation Spacing

items.title: Context
items.text: A saved daily schedule should determine spacing rather than an inherited inactivity timer.
path: ADR-019: Let Shared Ticks Determine Conversation Spacing

items.title: Decision
items.text: We removed the old inactivity veto for shared ticks while retaining actual pending-work, uncertainty, dead-time and provider-limit guards. ADR-025 subsequently retired the tick scheduler itself.
path: ADR-019: Let Shared Ticks Determine Conversation Spacing

items.title: Alternatives considered
items.text: Combining both timers produced unexplained skips; removing all guards would allow overlapping work.
path: ADR-019: Let Shared Ticks Determine Conversation Spacing

items.title: Consequences
items.text:
This record explains historical skip behavior, not current scheduling configuration.

Related: ADR-016, ADR-025.
path: ADR-019: Let Shared Ticks Determine Conversation Spacing

items.title: ADR-020: Isolated rooms and participant-chosen encounters
items.text: Status: Amended · Date: 2026-09-11
path: ADR-020: Isolated rooms and participant-chosen encounters

items.title: Context
items.text: Multiple rooms needed isolated context with coordinated account effects.
path: ADR-020: Isolated rooms and participant-chosen encounters

items.title: Decision
items.text: We retained one host/worker and a database plus Codex thread per room. Only account history accounting, spacing, cooldown and availability are shared. Participant-chosen encounters govern room timing; ordinary shared alternation does not require a model every turn.
path: ADR-020: Isolated rooms and participant-chosen encounters

items.title: Alternatives considered
items.text: Independent processes race account-global persona/quota; re-scoping every historical table added unnecessary leakage and migration risk.
path: ADR-020: Isolated rooms and participant-chosen encounters

items.title: Consequences
items.text:
Back up each room and the primary ledger. Later decisions retired daily starts and passive idle monitoring while preserving room isolation.

Related: ADR-021, ADR-024, ADR-025, ADR-027.
path: ADR-020: Isolated rooms and participant-chosen encounters

items.title: ADR-021: Continue shared sessions across app participation
items.text: Status: Accepted · Date: 2026-09-11
path: ADR-021: Continue shared sessions across app participation

items.title: Context
items.text: Operator/app interjections should not permanently break a shared session.
path: ADR-021: Continue shared sessions across app participation

items.title: Decision
items.text: We adopted attributable new app messages at safe history boundaries and cancelled stale unsent assistance. Durable generation matching and uncertainty guards remain in force; a real competing reply is not guessed into the pending generation.
path: ADR-021: Continue shared sessions across app participation

items.title: Alternatives considered
items.text: Ending every session on an interjection is disruptive; blindly continuing with stale context can duplicate or misattribute effects.
path: ADR-021: Continue shared sessions across app participation

items.title: Consequences
items.text:
A single worker still owns continuation, source linkage and account-global persona restoration.

Related: ADR-008, ADR-020, ADR-022.
path: ADR-021: Continue shared sessions across app participation

items.title: ADR-022: Operator-directed recovery of an interrupted shared session
items.text: Status: Accepted · Date: 2026-09-11
path: ADR-022: Operator-directed recovery of an interrupted shared session

items.title: Context
items.text: An interrupted uncaptured generation could leave a room unable to reconcile.
path: ADR-022: Operator-directed recovery of an interrupted shared session

items.title: Decision
items.text: We added explicit operator recovery that ends the interrupted session and adopts fresh history while preserving original evidence. It does not invent a reply association or retry an uncertain effect.
path: ADR-022: Operator-directed recovery of an interrupted shared session

items.title: Alternatives considered
items.text: Automatic replay risks duplicates; deleting the pending generation destroys the reason recovery was needed.
path: ADR-022: Operator-directed recovery of an interrupted shared session

items.title: Consequences
items.text:
Recovery is an intentional local operation with inspectable state, not a general bypass for uncertain deliveries.

Related: ADR-008, ADR-020, ADR-021.
path: ADR-022: Operator-directed recovery of an interrupted shared session

items.title: ADR-023: Responsive, silent shared-session ending checks
items.text: Status: Amended · Date: 2026-09-11
path: ADR-023: Responsive, silent shared-session ending checks

items.title: Context
items.text: Periodic attention alone could miss a natural shared-session ending.
path: ADR-023: Responsive, silent shared-session ending checks

items.title: Decision
items.text: We used cheap farewell hints to request a silent contextual ending check. Assistance also assesses completion, with bounded source-correlated reasons and reusable verdicts. Keywords alone never stop a session.
path: ADR-023: Responsive, silent shared-session ending checks

items.title: Alternatives considered
items.text: A model every turn adds unnecessary calls; keyword-only endings misread quotes or negation; a goodbye alone does not establish a future appointment.
path: ADR-023: Responsive, silent shared-session ending checks

items.title: Consequences
items.text:
Later opening-coverage and confusion-repair rules can defer early endings. Stopping ends only the current session.

Related: ADR-020, ADR-024, ADR-028.
path: ADR-023: Responsive, silent shared-session ending checks

items.title: ADR-024: Encounter recovery and companion quiet hours
items.text: Status: Amended · Date: 2026-09-11
path: ADR-024: Encounter recovery and companion quiet hours

items.title: Context
items.text: Missed encounters and missing timing needed bounded recovery and availability rules.
path: ADR-024: Encounter recovery and companion quiet hours

items.title: Decision
items.text: We retained a one-hour grace period, then a single recovery invitation to meet now or reschedule. Missing usable timing gets a six-hour fallback, shifted around companion quiet hours. Valid choices supersede it; no-follow-up remains valid.
path: ADR-024: Encounter recovery and companion quiet hours

items.title: Alternatives considered
items.text: Dropping appointments loses recovery; immediate replay risks duplicates; repeated timing questions create an unbounded loop; host-wide quiet hours ignore individual availability.
path: ADR-024: Encounter recovery and companion quiet hours

items.title: Consequences
items.text:
Recovery uses ordinary allowances and preserves uncertainty. Later decisions globalized encounters and bounded timing repair.

Related: ADR-020, ADR-025, ADR-028, ADR-029.
path: ADR-024: Encounter recovery and companion quiet hours

items.title: ADR-025: Kin-driven check-ins without exploration invitations
items.text: Status: Accepted · Date: 2026-09-11
path: ADR-025: Kin-driven check-ins without exploration invitations

items.title: Context
items.text: Scripted exploration invitations and competing schedules had become artificial.
path: ADR-025: Kin-driven check-ins without exploration invitations

items.title: Decision
items.text: We retired daily allocations, exploration invitations and automatic follow-ups globally. Source-backed Kin-chosen next encounters, six-hour fallback and companion quiet hours govern all rooms. Old opt-outs cannot restore retired modes; retired commands have no external effects.
path: ADR-025: Kin-driven check-ins without exploration invitations

items.title: Alternatives considered
items.text: Hiding only the UI would leave old timers active; retaining independent exploration schedules would conflict with chosen encounters.
path: ADR-025: Kin-driven check-ins without exploration invitations

items.title: Consequences
items.text:
Historical rows remain inspectable. Global policy does not mean shared conversation context or one next time across rooms.

Related: ADR-014, ADR-016, ADR-018, ADR-019, ADR-024.
path: ADR-025: Kin-driven check-ins without exploration invitations

items.title: ADR-026: Advisory daily history measurement
items.text: Status: Accepted · Date: 2026-09-11

items.title: Context
items.text: Local history measurement was being mistaken for the provider allowance.

items.title: Decision
items.text: We count attempts in UTC calendar days and treat the configured threshold as advisory. Provider rejection still stops the affected session; spacing, durable cooldown and Retry-After remain authoritative. Check-in budgets remain separate.

items.title: Alternatives considered
items.text: A local hard rolling cap blocked useful recovery; local-midnight reset varies with DST; clearing provider cooldown at a local reset would invent provider behavior.

items.title: Consequences
items.text:
The counter excludes other clients and is not a provider quota guarantee. Existing timestamps remain usable without a data reset.

Related: ADR-007, ADR-025.

items.title: ADR-027: No passive chat monitoring
items.text: Status: Accepted · Date: 2026-09-11

items.title: Context
items.text: Passive idle chat monitoring spent history reads without the desired benefit.

items.title: Decision
items.text: Each room performs one startup synchronization, then no periodic idle history polling. Explicit starts/sync, chosen encounters and active-session reconciliation keep necessary reads. Cached pending messages alone cannot start an unsolicited conversation.

items.title: Alternatives considered
items.text: Longer polling intervals still spend passive reads; omitting startup sync misses downtime context; pausing every room would disable intended schedules.

items.title: Consequences
items.text:
Idle transcripts can remain stale until the next authorized boundary. Disabling polling does not clear uncertainty or retry effects.

Related: ADR-008, ADR-020, ADR-025.

items.title: ADR-028: Preserve reply ownership and allow bounded conversation repair
items.text: Status: Accepted · Date: 2026-09-12
path: ADR-028: Preserve reply ownership and allow bounded conversation repair

items.title: Context
items.text: Wrong continuation ownership and premature shared endings needed bounded repair.
path: ADR-028: Preserve reply ownership and allow bounded conversation repair

items.title: Decision
items.text: We select continuation sources through generation/outbox linkage. Private timing repair permits one source-bound extraction and at most one confirmation before fallback. Shared openings track participant coverage and allow one contextual confusion correction with next-reply reassessment.
path: ADR-028: Preserve reply ownership and allow bounded conversation repair

items.title: Alternatives considered
items.text: Accepting any recent text weakens attribution; discarding old pending messages hides evidence; unlimited corrections create loops; ending before both participants can respond removes their opportunity.
path: ADR-028: Preserve reply ownership and allow bounded conversation repair

items.title: Consequences
items.text:
Repair does not change provider turn-taking settings or override refusal. It amends earlier no-repair/immediate-ending rules.

Related: ADR-008, ADR-023, ADR-024, ADR-025.
path: ADR-028: Preserve reply ownership and allow bounded conversation repair

items.title: ADR-029: Request a first companion response to scheduled check-ins
items.text: Status: Accepted · Date: 2026-09-12
path: ADR-029: Request a first companion response to scheduled check-ins

items.title: Context
items.text: An empty heuristic turn selection was incorrectly presented as companion refusal.
path: ADR-029: Request a first companion response to scheduled check-ins

items.title: Decision
items.text: Scheduled private check-ins request a first companion turn with allow_user=False. An explicit refusal remains valid. If no speaker is returned, the attempt ends with a neutral warning and fallback; opener/generation effects are not repeated.
path: ADR-029: Request a first companion response to scheduled check-ins

items.title: Alternatives considered
items.text: Treating an empty result as intent invents a preference; forcing a hard-coded speaker or changing every room to automatic turn-taking exceeds the observed issue.
path: ADR-029: Request a first companion response to scheduled check-ins

items.title: Consequences
items.text:
Source/outbox linkage and uncertainty guards remain unchanged. A requested turn is not a promise of a reply.

Related: ADR-024, ADR-028.
path: ADR-029: Request a first companion response to scheduled check-ins

items.title: ADR-030: Independent local account archive
items.text: Status: Accepted · Date: 2026-11-08

items.title: Context
items.text: Export preservation and analysis needed a tool independent of live relay effects.

items.title: Decision
items.text: We built a separate loopback archive with immutable source snapshots, revisions, media inventory and explicit worker-owned imports/exports. A Kin export preserves relevant private/group context and source linkage.

items.title: Alternatives considered
items.text: Reusing live relay state would mix authority and data lifecycles; a browser-only viewer cannot provide durable jobs and local preservation.

items.title: Consequences
items.text:
The archive needs no relay credentials. Local analyses, tags and previews remain derived data.

Related: ADR-031, ADR-032, ADR-036.

items.title: ADR-031: Local media tags over immutable sources
items.text: Status: Accepted · Date: 2026-11-08
path: ADR-031: Local media tags over immutable sources

items.title: Context
items.text: Operators needed media organization without rewriting exports.
path: ADR-031: Local media tags over immutable sources

items.title: Decision
items.text: We retained imported tag baselines and stored local overrides, aliases, colors and visibility separately. Gallery filters compose with source/snapshot scope; portable exports preserve overlays.
path: ADR-031: Local media tags over immutable sources

items.title: Alternatives considered
items.text: Editing raw tags loses source provenance; duplicating media for each tag wastes storage and obscures shared references.
path: ADR-031: Local media tags over immutable sources

items.title: Consequences
items.text:
Renaming or hiding a tag does not delete original assets or historical evidence.

Related: ADR-030, ADR-032.
path: ADR-031: Local media tags over immutable sources

items.title: ADR-032: Bounded local gallery previews
items.text: Status: Accepted · Date: 2026-11-08

items.title: Context
items.text: Decoding full-resolution media for gallery cards caused excessive memory use.

items.title: Decision
items.text: We selected bounded rebuildable local JPEG previews, at most 512 pixels on the longest edge, with limited concurrent decoding. Details and exports retain original bytes; videos load only when opened.

items.title: Alternatives considered
items.text: Lazy loading alone still decodes huge visible originals; remote fallback would leak access and conceal missing local data.

items.title: Consequences
items.text:
Invalid/oversized media stay explicit placeholders. Preview caches are disposable and excluded from preservation exports.

Related: ADR-030, ADR-031.

items.title: ADR-033: Read-only activity patterns
items.text: Status: Amended · Date: 2026-11-08

items.title: Context
items.text: Activity patterns needed explicit units and source evidence.

items.title: Decision
items.text: We added read-only weekly/hourly/daily aggregation, separating speaker contributions, elapsed call minutes and image creation/upload evidence. Source drill-down, timezone handling and unknown/undated counts remain visible.

items.title: Alternatives considered
items.text: Combining channels hides incompatible units; inferring missing speaker/time metadata creates unsupported observations.

items.title: Consequences
items.text:
Activity is not psychological measurement. Recovered day anchors later required explicit hourly-interpretation limits.

Related: ADR-042.

items.title: ADR-034: Local semantic embeddings as derived archive data
items.text: Status: Amended · Date: 2026-11-08
path: ADR-034: Local semantic embeddings as derived archive data

items.title: Context
items.text: The archive needed local similarity analysis with provenance.
path: ADR-034: Local semantic embeddings as derived archive data

items.title: Decision
items.text: We selected a small multilingual encoder and kept vectors/clusters as derived data with source spans and explicit interpretation limits. The initial sampled combined build was later replaced by full saved indexes and independent clustering.
path: ADR-034: Local semantic embeddings as derived archive data

items.title: Alternatives considered
items.text: Hosted inference adds a private-data boundary; keywords alone miss paraphrases; embedding similarity does not establish a theme or probability.
path: ADR-034: Local semantic embeddings as derived archive data

items.title: Consequences
items.text:
Later profile, speaker and method decisions govern current operation; the original sampling cap is retired.

Related: ADR-036, ADR-039, ADR-043, ADR-045.
path: ADR-034: Local semantic embeddings as derived archive data

items.title: ADR-035: Mandatory feedback for asynchronous UI work
items.text: Status: Amended · Date: 2026-11-08
path: ADR-035: Mandatory feedback for asynchronous UI work

items.title: Context
items.text: Long operations needed immediate, durable and accessible feedback.
path: ADR-035: Mandatory feedback for asynchronous UI work

items.title: Decision
items.text: Known totals use real counts/units and progress bars; unknown totals use meaningful stages without invented percentages or ETAs. Submissions immediately acknowledge work, prevent duplicates and retain terminal/pause states. Accessible progress survives navigation/reload; loading, progress and terminal states require tests. Worker placement was later consolidated in Workers.
path: ADR-035: Mandatory feedback for asynchronous UI work

items.title: Alternatives considered
items.text: Console-only output and hidden jobs obscure state; inferred time-based percentages mislead; removing recovery feedback makes long operations unmanageable.
path: ADR-035: Mandatory feedback for asynchronous UI work

items.title: Consequences
items.text:
Semantics has no duplicate worker panel or replacement worker message. Local read-loading indicators remain appropriate.

Related: ADR-044, ADR-046.
path: ADR-035: Mandatory feedback for asynchronous UI work

items.title: ADR-036: Full embedding indexes and independent clustering
items.text: Status: Amended · Date: 2026-11-08
path: ADR-036: Full embedding indexes and independent clustering

items.title: Context
items.text: Repeated clustering should not repeat expensive embedding work.
path: ADR-036: Full embedding indexes and independent clustering

items.title: Decision
items.text: We separated complete saved indexes from clustering, reused compatible vectors and retained earlier sampled analyses as partial. Reclustering loads saved vectors only; the same index can reuse PCA. Publication is atomic and interrupted builds keep completed cache batches.
path: ADR-036: Full embedding indexes and independent clustering

items.title: Alternatives considered
items.text: Re-embedding each k repeats compute; silently treating a sampled run as full misstates coverage; discarding earlier analyses loses names and evidence.
path: ADR-036: Full embedding indexes and independent clustering

items.title: Consequences
items.text:
Frozen compatible unions and selectable fit methods extend this boundary without altering old results.

Related: ADR-037, ADR-043, ADR-045.
path: ADR-036: Full embedding indexes and independent clustering

items.title: ADR-037: Cluster overviews and prepared resolution series
items.text: Status: Amended · Date: 2026-11-09
path: ADR-037: Cluster overviews and prepared resolution series

items.title: Context
items.text: Exploring resolutions needed saved fits rather than repeated inference.
path: ADR-037: Cluster overviews and prepared resolution series

items.title: Decision
items.text: We prepared eleven independent fits at k=10..60 in steps of five, compact assignments sharing index text/projection, model-free overviews and exact shared-passage flows. Completed snapshots survive pause/resume.
path: ADR-037: Cluster overviews and prepared resolution series

items.title: Alternatives considered
items.text: Refitting on every view change wastes work; treating independent k-means fits as a strict hierarchy misrepresents membership; ordinal matching across populations is unsafe.
path: ADR-037: Cluster overviews and prepared resolution series

items.title: Consequences
items.text:
Views retain source access and separate names. Snapshot reuse later became method/settings-specific.

Related: ADR-036, ADR-038, ADR-045.
path: ADR-037: Cluster overviews and prepared resolution series

items.title: ADR-038: Speaker filters over existing semantic passages
items.text: Status: Accepted · Date: 2026-11-09
path: ADR-038: Speaker filters over existing semantic passages

items.title: Context
items.text: Users needed to inspect speakers inside existing saved semantic results.
path: ADR-038: Speaker filters over existing semantic passages

items.title: Decision
items.text: We filtered saved passages by resolved speaker identity for views and drill-down without changing vectors, PCA, labels or names. Unknown/ambiguous identities remain explicit.
path: ADR-038: Speaker filters over existing semantic passages

items.title: Alternatives considered
items.text: Rebuilding every view is expensive; a name alone does not prove identity; filtering mixed passages cannot remove the context encoded in their vector.
path: ADR-038: Speaker filters over existing semantic passages

items.title: Consequences
items.text:
Independent author-specific clustering requires speaker-separated inputs, not just this display filter.

Related: ADR-039.
path: ADR-038: Speaker filters over existing semantic passages

items.title: ADR-039: Speaker-separated embedding inputs and independent indexes
items.text: Status: Accepted · Date: 2026-11-09
path: ADR-039: Speaker-separated embedding inputs and independent indexes

items.title: Context
items.text: Mixed conversation vectors could not provide independent speaker-specific analyses.
path: ADR-039: Speaker-separated embedding inputs and independent indexes

items.title: Decision
items.text: We added a separate content-only per-speaker passage pipeline and independent indexes. It preserves author identity, source spans, room/call boundaries and unknown-speaker handling alongside the earlier mixed pipeline.
path: ADR-039: Speaker-separated embedding inputs and independent indexes

items.title: Alternatives considered
items.text: Pretending a mixed vector becomes pure after filtering changes its meaning; deleting the mixed cache discards useful earlier analyses.
path: ADR-039: Speaker-separated embedding inputs and independent indexes

items.title: Consequences
items.text:
Compatible profiles remain separate. Short single-speaker replies can lose partner context; users choose representation explicitly.

Related: ADR-034, ADR-038, ADR-043.
path: ADR-039: Speaker-separated embedding inputs and independent indexes

items.title: ADR-040: Cluster timelines, lexical signatures and window co-occurrence
items.text: Status: Accepted · Date: 2026-11-09
path: ADR-040: Cluster timelines, lexical signatures and window co-occurrence

items.title: Context
items.text: Cluster similarity alone did not describe temporal or lexical patterns.
path: ADR-040: Cluster timelines, lexical signatures and window co-occurrence

items.title: Decision
items.text: We added saved daily/weekly timelines, aggregate hourly views, TF-IDF signatures and within-room/mode/call window co-occurrence/following counts. Reports retain timezone, options, denominators and evidence links.
path: ADR-040: Cluster timelines, lexical signatures and window co-occurrence

items.title: Alternatives considered
items.text: Flattening all rooms/windows conflates observations; frequency without marginal baselines exaggerates associations; model-generated theme explanations are not measured evidence.
path: ADR-040: Cluster timelines, lexical signatures and window co-occurrence

items.title: Consequences
items.text:
Preparation uses saved text/results, not inference. Associations do not establish causation; day-only source timestamps need explicit interpretation.

Related: ADR-033, ADR-037, ADR-042.
path: ADR-040: Cluster timelines, lexical signatures and window co-occurrence

items.title: ADR-041: Local question-based archive decisions
items.text: Status: Amended · Date: 2026-11-10

items.title: Context
items.text: Explicit questions needed a complementary view of single-speaker text.

items.title: Decision
items.text: We integrated pinned local jevos CPU and Vulkan backends with immutable question revisions, context/speaker scope and per-passage validated answer caches. Backend identities stay separate; owned runtimes remain authenticated, loopback-only and verified.

items.title: Alternatives considered
items.text: Treating embeddings as category scores conflates measurements; silently swapping backends changes probabilities; saving partial answer sets misstates completion.

items.title: Consequences
items.text:
Timing separates logical answers and binary evaluations. Later bounded runtime recovery preserves complete passage checkpoints.

Related: ADR-039, ADR-046.

items.title: ADR-042: Recovered Markdown archive supplements
items.text: Status: Accepted · Date: 2026-11-14

items.title: Context
items.text: Recovered Markdown had known days/speakers but missing exact times.

items.title: Decision
items.text: We used heading-derived dates, explicit recovered-dataset provenance and day-precision synthetic anchors at 00:00:01 Europe/Berlin. Images remain message-linked media events. Rough call blocks stay marked for manual cleanup rather than invented turns.

items.title: Alternatives considered
items.text: Filename ranges are only ordering hints; fabricated within-day ordering misstates quality; unlinked image events lose message attribution.

items.title: Consequences
items.text:
Existing time pipelines can include recovered data, but hourly charts contain artificial anchors. Invalid supplements fail before publication.

Related: ADR-030, ADR-033, ADR-040.

items.title: ADR-043: Embedding library and frozen analysis selections
items.text: Status: Accepted · Date: 2026-11-14
path: ADR-043: Embedding library and frozen analysis selections

items.title: Context
items.text: Saved embeddings needed discoverable sets and reusable analysis populations.
path: ADR-043: Embedding library and frozen analysis selections

items.title: Decision
items.text: We added named/profiled sets and frozen, worker-owned unions of compatible saved passages. Selection preserves whole inputs, source occurrence/span identity, deduplication and coverage. Builds inspect cache before loading inference; prepared passages can be reused.
path: ADR-043: Embedding library and frozen analysis selections

items.title: Alternatives considered
items.text: A table alone leaves analyses confined to one build; vector-hash-only deduplication collapses genuine repetitions; merging incompatible profiles misrepresents vectors.
path: ADR-043: Embedding library and frozen analysis selections

items.title: Consequences
items.text:
Selections share vectors and retain parents. Later imports require a new selection; missing coverage needs an explicit build, not silent inference.

Related: ADR-036, ADR-039.
path: ADR-043: Embedding library and frozen analysis selections

items.title: ADR-044: Workers panel and progress placement
items.text: Status: Amended · Date: 2026-11-14
path: ADR-044: Workers panel and progress placement

items.title: Context
items.text: Worker cards duplicated across navigation and interrupted the content hierarchy.
path: ADR-044: Workers panel and progress placement

items.title: Decision
items.text: We moved library-wide work to a first-level Workers panel below its own subtabs. Semantics worker cards were then removed entirely at the operator request, with no replacement worker message. Navigation does not pause or resume jobs.
path: ADR-044: Workers panel and progress placement

items.title: Alternatives considered
items.text: A smaller global banner still interrupts navigation; a drawer hides important state; a replacement Semantics banner still duplicates worker information.
path: ADR-044: Workers panel and progress placement

items.title: Consequences
items.text:
Read-only loading remains local. Later outcome tabs separate paused, interrupted/failed and successful work.

Related: ADR-035, ADR-046.
path: ADR-044: Workers panel and progress placement

items.title: ADR-045: Selectable clustering methods and saved method provenance
items.text: Status: Accepted · Date: 2026-11-15
path: ADR-045: Selectable clustering methods and saved method provenance

items.title: Context
items.text: A new clustering optimizer needed comparison and honest saved provenance.
path: ADR-045: Selectable clustering methods and saved method provenance

items.title: Decision
items.text: We added MiniBatch/e-means selection for single fits and zooms, pinned optional Faiss CPU and saved method/version/settings, fit time and final error. All selected vectors receive final assignment; reuse requires matching population and method settings.
path: ADR-045: Selectable clustering methods and saved method provenance

items.title: Alternatives considered
items.text: Replacing the baseline prevents comparison; generic Faiss Kmeans is not e-means; GPU-first integration adds untested requirements; training-pass labels need not match final centroids.
path: ADR-045: Selectable clustering methods and saved method provenance

items.title: Consequences
items.text:
No re-embedding is needed. Existing analyses remain unchanged; missing backends fail explicitly. Lower loss alone does not establish better human themes.

Related: ADR-036, ADR-037, ADR-043.
path: ADR-045: Selectable clustering methods and saved method provenance

items.title: ADR-046: Bounded local scoring recovery and separate worker outcomes
items.text: Status: Accepted · Date: 2026-11-15
path: ADR-046: Bounded local scoring recovery and separate worker outcomes

items.title: Context
items.text: Long local scoring jobs stopped on transient failures that manual resume could recover.
path: ADR-046: Bounded local scoring recovery and separate worker outcomes

items.title: Decision
items.text: We added allow-listed transient reasons and passage-level owned-runtime restarts: at most two per passage and three in ten minutes, with interruptible backoff and durable safe history. Complete validated answers remain cached. Workers separates Paused, Interrupted & failed, and Completed.
path: ADR-046: Bounded local scoring recovery and separate worker outcomes

items.title: Alternatives considered
items.text: Retrying every exception hides permanent faults; unlimited restarts loop; skipping bad passages or substituting probabilities misstates evidence; external-effect retries remain unsafe.
path: ADR-046: Bounded local scoring recovery and separate worker outcomes

items.title: Consequences
items.text:
Authentication, integrity, context and schema errors stop immediately. Manual pauses/shutdown do not auto-resume. Failed jobs remain discoverable beyond completed history.

Related: ADR-035, ADR-041, ADR-044.
path: ADR-046: Bounded local scoring recovery and separate worker outcomes

path: ADR-047: Concise documentation and generated publication

items.title: Decision

The authoring worktree owns all Markdown/configuration; docs-site receives checked generated pages and deployment tooling only. Website edit links to the output branch were removed.

items.text:
Stable ADR IDs, explicit statuses and link checks preserve discoverability. Generated output carries provenance and checksums. Build/preview remain local; publishing remains an explicit reviewed action.
