items.title: Models and methods
items.text:
Choose the representation and measurement before interpreting a visualization.

Method Purpose Reference E5 embeddings Similarity of saved text passages Embedding profile MiniBatch / e-means Exploratory grouping of those vectors Clustering jevos CPU / Vulkan Evidence for explicit questions about one speaker Scoring Codex relay/extraction Attributed assistance and bounded interpretation Memory

Inputs, model revision, passage construction, backend, questions and scope are part of result provenance. A model or representation change can change the interpretation even when the chart looks similar. Named entity recognition and calendar matching remain research, not installed analysis features.

items.title: Clustering settings and comparison
items.text:
Both methods fit every selected saved passage using squared Euclidean distance, float32 vectors and two CPU threads. They assign each passage to its nearest final centroid. Embedding generation is independent.

Setting MiniBatch K-means e-means Implementation scikit-learn MiniBatchKMeans Faiss CPU 1.16.0 NumpyEmeans Passes / seed 8 / 17 5 / 17 Initialization k-means++, one initialization Random sample without replacement Batch size max(256, 3 × trained clusters) Automatic upstream recipe Sampling cap None None Spherical mode Off Off

Install the optional archive-emeans extra to enable e-means. Unsupported/missing backends fail explicitly. An unavailable native fitter does not prevent viewing saved results. Distinct-vector count bounds the trained count; occupied groups can still be fewer. A one-vector case is marked as an analytic degenerate result.

Saved metadata includes method/version, seed, actual settings, assignment policy, fitting time and final mean squared distance. E-means also records its resolved recipe and cluster revival count. Fitting time excludes input loading, error evaluation, PCA, descriptions and database publication.

Compare the same frozen population, k and objective. Repeat timing under controlled load and review examples. Lower error and more even sizes do not establish better human themes. Cluster IDs differ across fits. Use shared membership to compare; the PCA map is not the space in which clustering error is measured.

References: e-means paper, pinned implementation.

items.title: Decision scoring backends
items.text:
Scoring uses jevos v5 locally through an owned, authenticated loopback runtime. Model files and runtimes are pinned and verified. CPU and Vulkan have separate cache identities; resume never silently changes backend.

Backend Current implementation Constraints CPU OpenVINO INT8, approximately 650 MB download Managed Windows x64 runtime Vulkan Q8 GGUF, llama.cpp b12255, approximately 981 MB Windows; observed GTX 1050 Ti and full GPU offload required

The GPU path currently selects the installed NVIDIA Vulkan manifest only in the owned child's environment. It requires all layers offloaded and allocated GPU model memory. There is no automatic CPU fallback or global driver change.

Vulkan uses a 4,096-token context budget and direct binary probabilities for yes/no answers, with choice/scale aggregation. An oversized prompt fails before saving that passage. Missing probabilities are errors, not zero scores.

New jobs default to four CPU threads or fewer when the machine has fewer logical processors; the upper limit is min(32, logical processors). Legacy jobs without a thread setting retain two. Threads affect new computation, not cache identity.

Timing metadata distinguishes logical answers, binary evaluations, startup, verification, inference and wrapper time. Different backends/quantizations can produce different probabilities. Scores are uncalibrated text classifications; review speaker attribution, context and examples. See workflow and recovery.

items.title: Embedding profile and passage construction
items.text:
The archive's installed encoder profile is multilingual E5-small, using the pinned Xenova conversion at revision 761b726dd34fb83930e26aab4e9ac3899aa1fa78. It uses an INT8 ONNX model, 384 dimensions, attention-mask mean pooling, L2 normalization and the query: prefix. Preparation downloads about 135 MB of public files; inference reads local files and sends no conversations to a hosted service.

Passages use a 380-token budget, at most six contributions, 15-minute chat buckets or five-minute call buckets. Room, chat/call mode and call identity remain separate. Long messages split with source character offsets. Undated text stays separate; date filters exclude it. Empty text, image prompts and configuration are outside this text analysis.

Single-speaker passages contain only their author's content. Mixed context passages retain conversation windows. A display-time speaker filter cannot convert mixed vectors into single-speaker embeddings.

Vector reuse requires the same model and exact prepared input. Frozen selections combine only compatible profiles, deduplicate source occurrences and report excluded boundary passages. Similarity is not a probability. See saved sets.

items.title: Operations and troubleshooting
items.text:
Use installation for first startup. Maintenance keeps source data and uncertain effects visible rather than attempting an automatic reset.

  • Back up, restore and upgrade.
  • Run and recover the relay.
  • Troubleshoot archive analyses.
  • Background workers and decision recovery.
  • Contributing and maintaining documentation.

Archive models are prepared explicitly. Restart the relevant host and reload its browser after updating code or UI files. A documentation/site rebuild does not restart either application. Local machine paths and deployment notes belong in the repository's internal runbook.

items.title: Archive
items.text:
Pause jobs and let active file/database publication reach a safe boundary before stopping or copying a library. Preserve its database, source snapshots, original media and annotations together. Include model files if offline startup is needed. Preview thumbnails and prepared-passage caches are rebuildable private derivatives.

A portable Kin ZIP is useful for a scoped transfer, but does not replace a backup of every library and its analysis database. Restore into a separate location and verify records, media gaps and saved analyses before replacing the working copy.

items.title: Relay
items.text: Use the CLI's backup --output <new-directory> operation for an online SQLite snapshot and schema/time/hash manifest. integrity inspects a database without starting relay work or migrating it. Back up every room database together with the primary account ledger; a secondary room alone cannot restore shared availability or provider accounting.

items.title: Upgrade
items.text: Back up first, pause, inspect in-flight work and stop the host safely. Install the intended code/dependencies, restart and reload the page. Numbered migrations preserve existing data. Never delete/recreate a database to resolve a version mismatch. Do not automatically replay sending or uncertain relay effects after restoration.

items.title: Maintain code and documentation
items.text:
The authoring repository is the single source for pages, configuration and publication tooling. The deployed site and docs-site branch are generated output; do not edit them. Public references live in public-docs/documentation/, journal entries in public-docs/journal/, and local evidence in docs/internal/ or ignored private storage.

Update the existing reference when behavior changes. Keep instructions current, move dated experiments to the Journal, and use an ADR only for a consequential architecture/behavior decision. Preserve its ID, alternatives and replacement links. Accepted design does not prove implementation or operator acceptance.

Pages declare kind, scope, status and review date. Proposed research must not appear as an installed feature. Keep one maintained explanation per subject and link to it. Avoid session transcripts, repeated test totals and obsolete setup instructions.

items.title: Verification
items.text:
Run the repository documentation checker, publication-boundary tests and strict site build. They validate links/anchors, navigation, page status and deployment output. Review prose and examples for privacy; automated checks cannot establish that an aggregate is anonymous.

Application tests use synthetic fixtures and bounded child processes. On Windows, never probe a PID with signal zero or send console control events from a test. Keep targeted checks small and the full-suite attempt under its 60-second limit. UI checks require npm ci --ignore-scripts before verification. A passing fixture is distinct from real-model, browser or operator acceptance.

See the repository publication guide for local Check/Build/Preview/Publish commands. Publishing is an explicit operation; cleaning or building docs does not deploy them.

items.title: Operate and recover the relay
items.text:
Run one combined serve host or the headless run alternative. Keep one owner for the account's effects and primary ledger. Sign-in task install/remove changes registration only; it does not start or stop a live relay.

Before stopping a terminal or hidden sign-in host, pause through the dashboard and wait for in-flight work. For a hidden Windows instance, use Task Scheduler to end the known task, then start it again. Forced termination is not graceful cancellation; inspect uncertainty on restart. Never terminate processes by executable name.

items.title: Inspect a stopped room
items.text:
1. Read the room's phase, command and activity evidence.
  2. Distinguish a deliberate pause, provider rejection, interrupted generation and uncertain delivery. Do not infer that a missing response means refusal.
  3. Use explicit history sync/recovery where appropriate. Shared-session recovery preserves original evidence while adopting fresh history.
  4. Resume only the intended room after uncertainty is resolved.

History use is measured per UTC day and shared across rooms. The warning threshold is advisory; real provider rejection still pauses the affected session, with account-wide spacing and durable cooldown. Resetting a counter does not clear a provider cooldown. Idle rooms do not monitor app chat after startup catch-up.

Diagnostics are bounded/redacted. Tests and troubleshooting must not expose credentials, raw private logs, authorization headers or browser storage.

items.title: Troubleshoot archive analyses
items.text:
Symptom Check Saved-set table stays empty Refresh filters, include hidden sets and confirm embedding-library.js loads. Restart/reload after updating the host. Completed builds already count as sets. Cannot combine sets Profiles must agree on model, pipeline and dimensions. Mixed and single-speaker inputs stay separate. Selection coverage is incomplete Inspect missing/partial records and boundary exclusions. Build the intended scope, then prepare a new frozen selection. Missing/corrupt vectors Run an explicit build/repair; clustering never silently drops them or starts inference. e-means unavailable Install the pinned optional extra, restart and reload. Saved results remain viewable. Media access denied A preserved export reference does not guarantee remote access. Keep the gap visible; avoid repeated unauthorized requests. Hourly peak near midnight Recovered data uses artificial day anchors. Inspect precision/source and use daily views. Decision job stopped Open Workers → Interrupted & failed; inspect error and Recovery history, then resume after correcting the cause. Vulkan prompt too long Shorten questions/context or start a new target-only run. The 4,096-token bound is enforced before saving the passage. Binary probability error The scorer did not provide valid yes/no token probabilities. Bounded runtime recovery applies; no fabricated score is saved. Runtime files changed / GPU offload not confirmed Verify the selected model/runtime and hardware. No automatic backend substitution occurs.

Decisions retain complete passage answers through interruption. Deliberate pauses and host shutdown are not automatic recovery triggers. See Workers for retry limits and scoring backends for supported hardware.

items.title: Research and roadmap
items.text:
These are investigation directions, not installed features or approved autonomous capabilities. Keep experimental claims tied to setup, date and evidence.

  • Named entities: people, places, organizations, identity resolution and possible combinations with themes and calendar context.
  • Calendar context: contextual associations with conversation activity.
  • Performance and hardware: validated limits and upgrade questions.
  • Agency roadmap: remaining design and acceptance work for the relay.

The Journal records selected dated experiments. Current operating instructions belong in feature/model guides, even when an experiment originally motivated them.

items.title: Calendar context ideas
items.text:
Ideas to explore; no calendar-analysis integration is implemented. A personal calendar can provide context for conversational activity without explaining it.

Candidate analyses:

  • Compare message volume, question scores or topic proportions around calendar events.
  • Look for weekday, travel, work and holiday patterns using explicit denominators.
  • Explore lagged relationships before/after events while separating conversation rooms.
  • Use reviewed entity/event matches as navigation to source evidence.

Use the intended primary calendar, preserve timezone, recurring-event identity, all-day events and missing/cancelled entries. A busy calendar is not a complete account of time use. Event titles and locations can be sensitive.

Define a question before inspecting many combinations, include comparison periods and minimum support, and distinguish exploratory findings from tested hypotheses. Recovered day-only chat dates support daily comparisons, not within-day ordering. Associations cannot establish causation or another person's internal state.

items.title: Named entity recognition
items.text:
Research; not implemented in the archive UI. NER identifies mentions of people, places, organizations and other categories. Linking mentions to persistent entities is a separate task; equal names do not establish identity.

Possible uses include entity search, timelines, topic/entity co-occurrence and calendar matching. Combine extracted mentions with source spans and speaker/context boundaries, not just embedding similarity. Keep uncertain aliases reviewable.

Approach Evaluation question Local conventional NER Are fast fixed-label models adequate for this multilingual text? Local span/label models Do configurable labels improve domain coverage at acceptable cost? Larger local language models Does context improve extraction and linking on stronger hardware? Hosted models Is a measured quality gain worth external processing of private text?

items.title: Candidates and related tasks
items.text:
Use spaCy German/English pipelines with reviewed rules as a CPU baseline. Evaluate configurable labels with urchade/gliner_multi-v2.1, fastino/gliner2-multi-v1 or fastino/gliner2.5-multi-v1. These are candidates from the research review, not installed archive components. A stronger workstation could support larger context models and more throughput; the existing decision scorer's Vulkan backend does not automatically accelerate NER.

NER finds a span such as a person's name. Entity resolution joins reviewed aliases across messages; entity linking maps a mention to a known record; coreference connects pronouns and descriptions. Relation/event extraction adds who did what with whom; temporal extraction normalizes dates such as “next Tuesday.” These need separate evaluation and provenance. Fiction, role-play and quoted speech need context labels before any personal timeline is inferred.

Cloud candidates include Azure NER, Google entity analysis, hosted structured-output language models, or a dedicated endpoint running an open model. Compare language coverage, measured extraction quality, billed input, retention and data-use terms for the exact service before choosing one.

items.title: First experiment
items.text:
Start with a small labelled evaluation across languages, short messages, fiction, quotes and ambiguous names. Measure mention precision/recall separately from entity linking. Store model/prompt versions and exact evidence spans. An LLM inference is not a verified biographical fact; avoid merging entities automatically.

Keep mention records separate from source messages, with offsets, category, language, model/version and review state. Cache by text plus extraction settings so unchanged messages need no repeated inference. Once quality is measured, combine entities with embedding clusters, question scores and calendar windows to explore context and co-occurrence. Distinguish Marc's statements from Hannah's and compare speakers separately.

Any cloud experiment requires an explicit data/authority decision. Hardware and model availability alone do not authorize sending conversation text elsewhere.

items.title: Performance and hardware investigations
items.text:
Investigation; hardware purchases are not selected architecture. Embedding generation, clustering and question scoring have different bottlenecks. Faster clustering does not establish faster model inference.

Measure native inference, startup, verification, tokenization, transport and database work separately. Reuse clients and model lifetimes, retain thread/backend settings, and compare the same input. Cache hits and fresh answers need separate counts.

The current managed scoring setup supports Windows CPU OpenVINO and a pinned Vulkan Q8 path validated for a GTX 1050 Ti. A small synthetic backend experiment showed a GPU speed advantage with probability differences; it is a dated measurement, not a guarantee for every question or future workstation.

A proposed Linux workstation needs its own runtime/model, memory/VRAM, driver and throughput evaluation. Budget estimates and tokens-per-second expectations should be dated and tested on representative prompts before purchase.

Separate bench findings: a PIR motion sensor worked to roughly four metres, including angled movement. The bare DHT11 test was deferred; a 433 MHz radio set was identified as radio rather than infrared. No sensor or wireless design was integrated into the relay. Keep these hardware experiments separate from current application requirements.

items.title: Deferred work and acceptance
items.text: This is the remaining direction, not a completed-feature list. Source and tests describe implementation; fixture coverage does not establish live acceptance.

items.title: Acceptance and operating evidence
items.text:
• Reconfirm real-browser/native-dialog and Windows startup/recovery behavior after changes.
  • Evaluate real-model attribution, refusal, timing extraction and shared-session endings.
  • Validate missed appointments, quiet hours and recovery on the intended always-on host.
  • Review memory extraction quality and operator acceptance before broader automatic use.

Live Kindroid tests require explicit operator authority and a disposable conversation. Do not treat a historical test count or a partially completed checklist as approval.

items.title: Agency design
items.text:
The proposed garden distinguishes stable Roots, sustained Growing interests and provisional Passing observations. The implementation currently supports observation and versioning, not automatic identity promotion or project execution.

Manual Root bootstrap still needs agreed wording, ownership, provenance and backup. Automated self-change needs separate companion consent and operator authority, versioned proposals, exact preview, confirmation and rollback. Broader autonomous work needs budgets, stopping rules and an explicit capability grant.

Retired daily schedules and exploration invitations are not backlog items to re-enable. New breadth/discovery work requires a fresh design consistent with current Kin-chosen encounters. NER, calendar matching and new hardware remain separate research candidates.

items.title: Archive workflow
items.text:
The archive imports exported data into a local library. It does not connect to live Kindroid chat or use relay credentials.

Main tab Use Records Search messages and calls; inspect source provenance Media Browse local images and exported references; manage tags Activity Inspect counts, dates and daily rhythms Semantics Manage embeddings, cluster saved passages and inspect patterns Decisions Score saved single-speaker passages against defined questions Workers Inspect submissions, progress, pause/resume and results Settings Select snapshots, revisions and archive scope Kin Settings Inspect exported companion configuration

Select a companion or group in the sidebar. Source, date and snapshot controls set the browsing/build scope. A saved embedding set or analysis retains its own scope; navigation does not silently change its membership.

Use Library & jobs for explicit imports, downloads and exports. A standalone Kin library preserves bundled media and annotations, and accepts recovered supplements for its existing companion. Ordinary additional exports belong in a cumulative library.

Follow data and recovery, media, embeddings, clustering, Decisions or Workers. Sources remain immutable; derived annotations and analyses stay separate.

items.title: Clusters and visualizations
items.text:
Select a saved embedding set in Semantics → Settings or use a library row. In Clusters, choose Clustering method, a count from 2 to 100, and Cluster saved embeddings. This reads saved vectors and performs no encoding. Each analysis keeps its own names, assignments, method/settings and error.

MiniBatch K-means is the default. Optional e-means · Faiss CPU uses the pinned Faiss implementation. See method settings. The requested count is an upper bound; some groups can remain empty.

Prepare zoom · 10–60 clusters saves eleven independent fits in steps of five. Zooms preserve their method and completed snapshots through pause/resume. Reuse requires the same population and relevant method settings. Different methods cannot supply each other's snapshots. Resolution changes use saved results.

View Interpretation Theme overview / bubbles Relative group sizes and related families Similarities Cosine similarities of cluster summaries Resolution flows Exact shared-passage membership between saved fits Passage map PCA projection; proximity is only a two-dimensional approximation Patterns Timelines, lexical signatures and shared-window co-occurrence

Clusters are not a strict hierarchy. IDs and colors do not correspond across different fits; use shared passages and examples to compare them. The same index can reuse its PCA coordinates across methods.

Speaker filters inspect existing results without refitting. Mixed passages can still contain partner context; use single-speaker embeddings for an independent author-specific cluster space. Pattern reports retain timezone, window size and scope. Counts/share, minimum support and source drill-down are essential when comparing periods.

items.title: Import, recover and export
items.text: Import monthly JSONL exports into a cumulative library. Equivalent copies are folded using source identity while revisions and source locations are preserved. Choose a snapshot for its historical view, or cumulative/current data for the latest available revisions. Reimporting the same export is idempotent.

items.title: Recovered history
items.text:
The recovery converter reads strict day/speaker headings in Markdown. Filenames are ordering hints, not date authority. Inspect ambiguous voice-call blocks by hand before conversion; rough transcripts are not invented individual turns.

Recovered records retain data_source: recovered, dataset/source provenance and timestamp_precision: day. Known days use 00:00:01 Europe/Berlin as a synthetic timestamp so existing time-based analyses can include them. It is not an observed message time. Hourly charts therefore contain an artificial concentration that changes displayed hour with timezone.

Images remain attached to their source message and are also represented as linked media events. The recovery format records sender and origin evidence, including recovered AI selfies and user uploads. Exact within-day sending times remain unknown.

Convert with python -m kindroid_archive.recovery --input-dir path-to-markdown --kin EXISTING_KIN_ID --exclude rough-call-file.md --output recovered.jsonl (use a new output path). Omit --output for a validation preview. Then select the companion and use Library & jobs → Import recovered JSONL. Imports validate before publication; invalid supplements do not publish a partial snapshot. Source edits create revisions.

items.title: Export and portability
items.text: Export one Kin as JSONL or a portable ZIP with its relevant private/group context, source links, local tags and media manifest. Missing media remain explicit gaps. Open an unpacked ZIP using the standalone bundle option; the main library remains separate. See backup and upgrade before moving libraries.

items.title: Question based scoring
items.text:
Decisions scores saved single-speaker passages against explicit questions using local jevos inference. It does not require clustering first. Review examples before running a large analysis; probabilities are model estimates about text.

  1. In Settings, choose a saved single-speaker set, speakers and CPU/Vulkan backend.
  2. Prepare/verify the selected runtime if needed. Set threads for new jobs.
  3. In Question + scoring, edit definitions and Save new revision.
  4. Start a chronological 100/300-passage pilot or all eligible saved passages.
  5. In Heatmaps, inspect timelines, hourly patterns, co-occurrence and following patterns together with counts and passage evidence.

Independent yes/no questions can overlap. Choice questions distribute probability over competing alternatives. Ordered scales preserve a distribution and show a normalized expected level. Include an unclear/other option where appropriate.

Optional preceding context helps interpret the target; it is not the classified speaker's own statement. Runs freeze questions, context, backend, threads and scope. Resume uses that saved definition, even if current screen settings differ. Validated passage answers are cached; CPU and Vulkan use separate identities.

Progress and recovery controls are in Workers. Transient scorer failures receive bounded runtime recovery; completed passages remain saved. See models and limits and troubleshooting.

Scores are not calibrated psychological measurements. Fiction, quotations, sarcasm, short replies and language differences affect results. Empty periods mean no scored observations. Co-occurrence and following rates do not establish causation.

items.title: Manage embedding sets
items.text: A completed embedding build is already a saved set. Semantics → Embeddings lists names, dates, model/settings, representation, vector counts and usage. Search or filter the table; rename sets or hide them without deleting vectors.

items.title: Encode new conversations
items.text:
1. Choose companion, source and date scope. All available dates overrides dates only.
  2. Choose single-speaker content or mixed context, chat/calls and optional speakers.
  3. Optionally run Check work before encoding for cached/missing counts.
  4. Choose Build / update all embeddings and follow the job in Workers.

Builds encode only missing compatible inputs. Saved preparation avoids repeating tokenization after a check or interruption. Completed vector batches survive pause; an index is published atomically when complete. There is no passage-count sampling cap.

items.title: Reuse saved embeddings
items.text:
Create set from saved embeddings opens the selection controls in Clusters. Choose a compatible profile, name and filters, then Prepare analysis selection. Leave automatic selection enabled for all compatible visible builds, or check sets manually in the library. Preparing a selection performs no embedding inference.

A profile requires the same model, passage pipeline and dimensions. Single-speaker and mixed-context sets cannot be combined. Whole passages crossing a filter boundary are excluded and counted; their text is never trimmed beneath an existing vector.

The resulting frozen set stores its parent sets, deduplication and source coverage. It becomes the clustering input and appears in the table. Inspect missing/partial coverage, build that scope if needed, then prepare a new selection. Incomplete coverage requires explicit permission before clustering. A frozen selection does not expand after later imports.

See embedding methods and clustering.

items.title: Media and activity
items.text:
Media opens on Kindroid creations. Select User uploads, Other / unknown or All sources and combine them with date, tag and local-file filters. A card opens the original file and source details. The gallery never automatically fetches a remote image to replace an unavailable local asset.

Cards use rebuildable JPEG previews of at most 512 pixels on the longest edge. Original files and export bytes are preserved. Download unavailable media explicitly in Library; an exported reference can still return access denied. A visible image in the Kindroid app does not establish downloadable export access.

Tags have an imported baseline and local overrides. Rename, hide/delete or restore local tags without rewriting source records. Shared media are deduplicated; a media asset can have both creation and user-share evidence. AI attribution alone does not prove ordinary native attachments were generated.

items.title: Activity
items.text:
Weekly history, daily hourly calendars and totals separate chat/call contributions, elapsed call time, created images and user uploads. Change timezone and inspect a cell's source records before interpreting it. Call minutes measure elapsed call time, not speaking time.

Counts use the selected revisions and scope. Missing dates, unknown speakers and excluded duplicates are disclosed. Recovered day anchors distort hourly patterns; use day/week views or filter recovered data for analyses requiring actual hours.

items.title: Memory and garden
items.text:
Agent context memory is Codex's attributed understanding, separate from Kindroid memory and the companion's identity. Statements retain source evidence, speaker, interpretation and correction history. Contradictions and uncertain identity matches require review rather than silent merging.

Capture and automatic context injection are opt-in. Semantic extraction uses an isolated, read-only Codex turn with tools disabled and bounded captured text. The complete output must validate before a batch is committed. This consumes the configured service's usage allowance. Optional local semantic retrieval has a versioned cache and a lexical fallback; it is distinct from archive E5 embeddings.

The observational garden retains Passing candidates and immutable versions. Local archive/restore and reasoned administrative annotations preserve attribution; an operator annotation is not a companion preference.

Roots and Growing express the longer-term design. Storage does not establish an enabled promotion, identity-editing or project-execution workflow. Automatic promotion, prompt projection and broader self-change remain deferred. Manual Root bootstrap requires agreed wording, provenance, backup and ownership.

Read identity and authority and the roadmap before proposing new agency behavior.

items.title: Relay rooms and encounters
items.text:
The relay connects configured Kindroid rooms to a persistent Codex thread through one worker. Rooms retain separate messages, memory, approvals and agent context. They share account-level request spacing and provider cooldowns.

Start with the dashboard paused. Select a room using room navigation, inspect its state, then use the intended explicit conversation/check-in command. The shared room alternates configured companions; mentions can request attributed Codex assistance. Codex output keeps the [CODEX]: prefix.

items.title: Scheduling
items.text:
Current rooms use source-backed Kin-chosen next encounters, with a six-hour fallback when usable timing is absent and per-companion quiet hours. Explicit no-follow-up choices remain valid. Missed appointments offer meeting now or rescheduling; they do not replay uncertain work.

Daily tick allocations, shared daily-start controls and exploration invitations are retired. Old configuration cannot restore those modes. Historical evidence remains inspectable.

Each room synchronizes history once on host startup. Idle rooms do not passively poll chat. Explicit sync/start, scheduled encounters and active-session recovery retain necessary history access. The local account counter is advisory and resets at midnight UTC; provider limits, spacing and cooldowns remain authoritative.

items.title: Recovery and authority
items.text:
Inspect interrupted or uncertain operations before continuing. Explicit shared-session recovery can adopt fresh history without guessing an uncaptured reply association. Never retry an uncertain delivery merely because its outcome is inconvenient.

Local approval governs consequential external actions. Companion consent and operator authority remain separate. See architecture, safety and relay operations.

items.title: Workers and recovery
items.text:
Workers is the main tab for background work across the library. Archive filters do not limit this list or stop jobs. Semantics has no duplicate worker panel or replacement worker status message. Read-only table/map loading stays local.

Tab Contents All workers Active and stopped jobs plus recent successful work Running & queued Work currently executing or waiting Paused Deliberate pauses Interrupted & failed Work requiring inspection or resume Completed Successful jobs only

All failed/interrupted jobs remain available beyond the most recent 30 completed jobs. Cards show actual stage totals, units, errors and results. Unknown totals use an indeterminate indicator. Pause/resume acts at supported boundaries; queued work can pause before it starts. Export downloads appear on completed export jobs.

items.title: Decision scorer recovery
items.text:
Transient local CPU/Vulkan failures close the owned runtime and retry the same passage. Limits are two restarts per passage and three within ten minutes, with one/three-second interruptible waits. Worker state stays running during recovery. History retains fixed causes, timestamps, passage numbers and outcomes.

Completed passage answers remain linked and are skipped. Incomplete answers never enter the cache. Resume preserves the original backend and questions. Recovery does not switch CPU/GPU, download models or skip evidence.

Authentication, context limits, changed model files and invalid answer schemas stop immediately. Manual pause/shutdown does not trigger automatic restart. If limits are exhausted, inspect history, correct the cause and explicitly resume.

This local inference policy does not apply to the relay's uncertain external effects.

items.title: Journal
items.text:
Dated notes preserve the question, the approach, the observation and what remains uncertain. Later entries can refine an earlier conclusion without rewriting the history of the experiment.

items.title: Why speaker boundaries come first
items.text: 10 November 2026 · Embeddings and attribution

items.title: The question
items.text:
Can an embedding map reveal differences between speakers when each embedded passage contains contributions from several of them?

That was a problem in the initial passage construction. Filtering an already embedded mixed passage by speaker changes which passages are visible. It does not remove the other speaker's words from the vector that was computed earlier.

items.title: The change
items.text:
A separate embedding pass now constructs passages from a single speaker's text. An index can include several speakers while retaining separate passages, or can be built for one selected speaker. Mixed-context indexes remain available for questions where conversational context is useful.

This moves attribution into the input representation, before vector construction. The embedding model is only one part of the method; passage construction changes what its output represents.

items.title: The trade-off
items.text:
Consider this invented exchange:

Speaker A: Would a walk help you relax? Speaker B: Yes.

The isolated reply carries little topical information. The mixed exchange gives it meaning, but also includes an activity suggested by another speaker. These representations answer different questions. Keeping both makes that choice explicit instead of hiding it in a filter.

items.title: What this supports
items.text:
Speaker-separated indexes make it possible to compare thematic patterns while knowing whose words entered each vector. They do not establish that similar vectors reflect the same intention, feeling or personal trait.

For explicit question scoring, the next step is to distinguish the target speaker from any preceding context, then inspect examples where those two point in different directions. See questions and patterns.

items.title: Testing Vulkan for question scoring
items.text: 10 November 2026 · Local inference and performance

items.title: The question
items.text:
Could the existing GTX 1050 Ti accelerate local question scoring enough to make larger experiments more practical?

The first managed decision backend used jevos v5 with OpenVINO INT8 on the CPU. A prototype tested the public Q8 GGUF weights with a pinned llama.cpp Vulkan runtime before adding a GPU option to the archive tool.

items.title: What was compared
items.text:
The test used seven synthetic passages. It covered independent yes/no questions, a three-way choice, a three-level scale, three 558-character targets with eleven questions each, and a longer 1,390-character target. GPU and CPU model lifetimes were sequential. CPU inference used four threads.

The machine had a Ryzen 5 3550H, about 5.9 GiB usable system RAM and a GTX 1050 Ti with 4 GB VRAM. The GPU path used llama.cpp b12255 and jevos v5 Q8. It read the binary answer-token distribution and reproduced option/scale aggregation; it did not ask a chat model to invent percentages.

Measurement Vulkan Q8 OpenVINO CPU Median of three 558-character, eleven-question passages 1.40 s 3.86 s Longer target, eleven questions 1.59 s 5.10 s Total scoring across all seven passages, excluding startup 6.91 s 19.74 s

The representative median was about 2.8 times faster. All 49 compared labels agreed, using a 0.5 threshold for yes/no and the largest probability for choice/scale. The largest probability difference was 7.96 percentage points. Agreement is not the same as independently measured accuracy or calibration.

items.title: The surprises
items.text:
The laptop's default Vulkan enumeration exposed the integrated AMD GPU. Selecting the installed NVIDIA Vulkan driver for the owned child process resolved startup without changing global driver settings.

Prompt construction also mattered: adding a start token twice was caught during the prototype and corrected. A backend comparison is only useful when the input format and scoring semantics are comparable.

items.title: From prototype to an option in the tool
items.text:
The managed GPU integration added a backend selector, separate CPU/GPU cache identities, saved runtime/model provenance and checks for actual full layer offload. Existing runs keep their original backend on resume. It also preserves job progress, cancellation and completed passage answers.

A subsequent synthetic worker check scored 39 logical answers from 48 binary evaluations across three passages. It paused, closed the runtime, resumed and completed, then reused all three passages on a repeated run.

items.title: Limits and next questions
items.text:
First-use timing varied: an earlier GPU trial took 6.15 seconds for its first eleven-question target before later targets became faster. The desktop was live, the sample was small and the text was synthetic. These numbers are not an ETA for an entire archive.

The next useful measurements are longer varied runs, system memory pressure and reviewed examples close to classification thresholds. CPU and GPU probabilities remain separate experimental results.
